[1] These shoppers anticipated spending an average of $831 each. [1] The survey, which polled over 2,000 U.S. adults, also highlighted that 74% of these holiday shoppers planned to use a credit card for their gift purchases, expecting to charge an average of $680. [1] Furthermore, 56% of shoppers indicated that inflation would prevent them from buying as many gifts as they would like. [1] <2> The Salvation Army's annual Angel Tree program is a nationwide initiative that provides Christmas gifts to children aged 12 and under from low-income families. [1, 4] The program, which began in 1979, aims to provide new clothing and toys to more than one million children each year, often in collaboration with corporate partners like Walmart, with whom they have worked for over four decades. [2, 12] Corporations, organizations, and individuals can participate by "adopting" an angel from trees set up in malls and other locations or online and purchasing items from the child's wish list. [9, 12] While specific dates vary by location, the application and registration process for families in need generally begins in September and October. [1, 4, 8, 10] Donors can then adopt angels and drop off gifts in the subsequent months, with distribution to families typically occurring in the week before Christmas. [2, 4] <3> A report from automation company Celigo, titled the “2023 Holiday Shopping Trends Report,” indicates a shift in consumer behavior for the holiday season. The survey of over 1,000 U.S. consumers revealed that 75% plan to conduct most of their holiday shopping online. Many consumers are starting earlier, with nearly half intending to begin by October. Specifically, over 50% of Gen X and 50% of millennial shoppers planned to start looking for deals in September and October. The report, announced on September 5, 2023, also found that consumers are more price-conscious, with 80% planning to spend less on gifts and nearly half aiming to stay under a $1,000 budget. Consequently, 26% of those surveyed intended to bypass Black Friday entirely. <4> A Bazaarvoice consumer survey of over 1,000 American shoppers, published in August 2023, offered insights into the 2023 holiday shopping season. The study revealed a strong preference for in-store shopping, with 81% of consumers planning to shop at brick-and-mortar locations. Social media was identified as a major channel for product discovery, as 63% of shoppers expected to find new items on these platforms. Furthermore, user-generated content was shown to be highly influential, with 74% of shoppers agreeing that reviews impact their purchasing decisions. The report also identified the most popular gift categories, which included apparel (70%), games and toys (51%), and electronics (47%). The research, conducted by Dynata in August 2023, indicated that the shopping season had already begun for many, with 24% of consumers starting in August or earlier. <5> Walmart announced its 2023 "Top Toys List" on August 22, 2023, a week earlier than the previous year. The list featured 55 of the most anticipated toys for the holiday season, with a significant focus on affordability by including over 25 toys priced under $25. The selection was heavily influenced by major entertainment and pop culture moments, highlighting toys from franchises like "Barbie," "Transformers: Rise of the Beasts," and "PAW Patrol." The list was organized into categories including "25 Under $25," "Blockbuster Hits," "90s Nostalgia," and others designed to encourage family activities and STEAM learning. <6> A report by Practical Ecommerce published on August 8, 2023, predicts that U.S. holiday spending during the 2023 season, starting around November 1, 2023, will grow by less than 5% due to inflation and economic concerns. The forecast also anticipates a significant rise in 'Buy Now, Pay Later' financing, expected to peak at a record 9% of online orders the week before Christmas, an increase from 7% in 2022. Additionally, the report suggests that retailers will continue to offer deep discounts to appeal to price-sensitive consumers, repeating tactics that were successful in the previous year. <7> Hallmark announced its 2023 Keepsake Ornament Premiere event, marking the 50th anniversary of Hallmark Keepsake Ornaments. The event, which provided the first opportunity for the public to purchase from a collection of over 250 new ornaments, ran from July 15-23. Members of the Hallmark Keepsake Ornament Club received early in-store shopping access on July 14. As part of the celebration, exclusive artist signing events were held at select Hallmark Gold Crown stores from July 21-22. <8> Christmas Tree Shops announced it would be liquidating all of its approximately 70 remaining stores after the company defaulted on a $45 million bankruptcy loan. This decision, reported around July 3-5, 2023, marked a final step after the company had initially filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 5, 2023, with a plan to reorganize and close only a few underperforming stores. The failure to meet the terms of its loan led to the termination of the financing and the subsequent agreement to liquidate all locations unless a last-minute buyer emerged. The company had been sold by the now-defunct Bed Bath & Beyond to Handil Holdings in 2020. The final day of business for all remaining stores was announced as August 12, 2023.

metadata.original_text: This time series records christmas gifts data in the web search domain, with a collection frequency of weekly, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2024-02-18 to 2024-05-05. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The National Retail Federation (NRF) announced on January 18, 2024, that core retail sales for the 2023 holiday season, defined as November 1 to December 31, grew by 3.8% over the previous year to a new record of $964.4 billion. This growth aligned with the NRF's forecast of a 3% to 4% increase, demonstrating notable consumer resilience amid inflation and higher interest rates. The total sales surpassed the 2022 record of $929.5 billion. A significant portion of this growth was driven by online and other non-store sales, which increased by 8.2% to $276.8 billion, also falling within the NRF's projected range of 7% to 9% growth for that category. <2> A report from CivicScience, published on January 9, 2024, revealed that expected holiday gift returns for the 2023 season saw a 47% increase compared to 2022. [2] The data, collected at the end of the 2023 holiday season, indicated that nearly one-in-three U.S. adults who received a gift were planning to make a return or exchange. [2] Among different demographics, Gen Z adults were identified as the generation most likely to be returning their gifts. [2] <3> Mastercard SpendingPulse released a report indicating that U.S. holiday retail sales, excluding automotive, for the period of November 1 to December 24, 2023, saw an increase of 3.1% compared to the same period in 2022. [1, 2, 3, 4, 8] This growth rate was slower than the 7.6% increase observed in the previous year and slightly below the 3.7% that Mastercard had forecasted for the season. [3, 8] The data, which is not adjusted for inflation, shows that online sales were a significant driver of this growth, increasing by 6.3%, while in-person sales grew more modestly at 2.2%. [1, 2, 5, 6] Spending in restaurants was particularly strong, showing a 7.8% rise year-over-year. [3, 4, 5] The apparel category also saw growth of 2.4%. [3, 4, 5] However, not all sectors experienced an increase; sales for electronics and jewelry saw slight declines of 0.4% and 2.0% respectively. [5, 8] <4> A survey by the National Retail Federation (NRF) and Prosper Insights & Analytics, announced on November 20, 2023, identified the most popular gift categories for the 2023 holiday season. [1] The top five categories were clothing, chosen by 56% of consumers, followed by gift cards at 44%, toys at 37%, books/video games/other media at 31%, and food/candy at 29%. [1] When it came to gifts for children, the survey found that Legos were the top choice for boys, with Hot Wheels and cars also being popular. [1, 3] For girls, Barbie was the most popular gift, followed by dolls and Legos. [1, 3] The survey of 8,424 adult consumers was conducted from November 1 to November 6, 2023. [3] <5> The Toy Retailers Association officially released its predictions for the top-selling Christmas toys of 2023 on November 8, 2023, expanding its traditional list to 20 items. [1] The selection, branded as DreamToys, is curated by an independent panel of toy retailers and experts and is considered an authoritative forecast for the holiday season. [1] The 2023 list included a variety of toys, such as the Barbie Pop Reveal, Beast Lab, and several interactive digital pets like the Bitzee Interactive Pet, Little Live Pets My Puppy’s Home, and Mintid Dog-E. [3] Recognizing the continued popularity of major franchises, the list also featured products like the LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Castle & Grounds, a LEGO Star Wars Ahsoka Starship, and the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Movie Pizza Fire Van. [4, 2] <6> A NerdWallet survey, conducted online by The Harris Poll from August 17-21, 2023, found that 85% of Americans, equivalent to nearly 222 million people, intended to buy holiday gifts in 2023. [1] These shoppers anticipated spending an average of $831 each. [1] The survey, which polled over 2,000 U.S. adults, also highlighted that 74% of these holiday shoppers planned to use a credit card for their gift purchases, expecting to charge an average of $680. [1] Furthermore, 56% of shoppers indicated that inflation would prevent them from buying as many gifts as they would like. [1] <7> The Salvation Army's annual Angel Tree program is a nationwide initiative that provides Christmas gifts to children aged 12 and under from low-income families. [1, 4] The program, which began in 1979, aims to provide new clothing and toys to more than one million children each year, often in collaboration with corporate partners like Walmart, with whom they have worked for over four decades. [2, 12] Corporations, organizations, and individuals can participate by "adopting" an angel from trees set up in malls and other locations or online and purchasing items from the child's wish list. [9, 12] While specific dates vary by location, the application and registration process for families in need generally begins in September and October. [1, 4, 8, 10] Donors can then adopt angels and drop off gifts in the subsequent months, with distribution to families typically occurring in the week before Christmas. [2, 4] <8> The United States Postal Service (USPS) launched its 111th annual Operation Santa program, a charity initiative where the public can 'adopt' letters written to Santa by children and families and send them gifts. For the first time, in response to public requests for more time, the program began accepting letters to Santa on September 18, 2023, which was before Black Friday. The process for the public to adopt these letters opened on November 20, 2023, with the final day for sending letters to Santa being December 11, 2023. The last day to adopt a letter was December 18. <9> A report from automation company Celigo, titled the “2023 Holiday Shopping Trends Report,” indicates a shift in consumer behavior for the holiday season. The survey of over 1,000 U.S. consumers revealed that 75% plan to conduct most of their holiday shopping online. Many consumers are starting earlier, with nearly half intending to begin by October. Specifically, over 50% of Gen X and 50% of millennial shoppers planned to start looking for deals in September and October. The report, announced on September 5, 2023, also found that consumers are more price-conscious, with 80% planning to spend less on gifts and nearly half aiming to stay under a $1,000 budget. Consequently, 26% of those surveyed intended to bypass Black Friday entirely.
